Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 68
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: European
  relationship_status: Married
  occupation: Politician
  trauma_type: Life-threatening accident
  pcl5: 73

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Discomfort: Feeling uncomfortable, Olfactory (Alcohol): Alcohol smell, Crash Imagery: Cars hit by accident
  Maladaptive Strategies: Self-Blame Rumination: I dwell on what I have done wrong, Rumination: Self-Blame: repeatedly blame myself for what happened, Avoid Driving: Driving or being a passenger in a vehicle
  Threat: Waking Alert: I wake during the night to check whether I am safe, Threat in Silence: Unusual silence makes me feel something dangerous is about to happen, Concentration: Having difficulty concentrating
  Memory: Snapshot Memory: I remember the frightening event as a few moments, and each moment is a picture in my mind., Cannot Explain Clearly: When I try to explain what happened I lose the thread and cannot finish, Pain Recall: When the memory returns I feel physical pain in the same parts of my body as during the event
  Negative Appraisals: Character Blame: The event happened to me because of the sort of person I am, Hypervigilance: I have to be on guard all the time, Exposed to Others: I feel that others can see what happened to me just by looking at me

Vignette:
John, a 68-year-old European-American politician, experienced a life-threatening accident several months ago that has left him grappling with profound psychological distress. John had always been active and engaged in his community until he was involved in a severe car crash on one of his campaign stops. The accident left him feeling shaken to his core and struggling to cope with the aftermath. The traumatic event occurred during an evening rally when John's driver lost control of their vehicle, leading to a devastating collision with another car that veered into their lane due to alcohol-impaired driving. John vividly remembers the moments just before impact: the blinding headlights, the screeching tires, and the overwhelming smell of burning rubber and fuel. These memories now resurface in snapshots whenever he encounters triggers like the smell of alcohol or images of vehicles crashing on the news. Since the accident, John has been ruminating intensely about his role in what happened. He frequently thinks about whether there was anything he could have done differently to prevent the crash, leading him to blame himself repeatedly for not being more vigilant. This self-blame exacerbates his distress and makes it difficult for him to concentrate on his work and personal life. John’s hyper-vigilance has become a pervasive aspect of his daily routine. He often wakes up in the middle of the night feeling that something dangerous is about to happen, particularly if he hears an unusual silence around him. This heightened state of alertness makes it hard for him to relax or trust his surroundings, and he avoids driving altogether out of fear that another accident could occur. John's memory of the event remains fragmented in his mind; he recalls certain moments as distinct snapshots, each one filled with intense physical sensations. When these memories resurface, John often experiences physical pain in the same areas where he was injured during the crash. This pain adds to his sense of vulnerability and unease, making it even harder for him to focus on tasks at hand. John's spouse has noticed significant changes in his behavior over the past few months. He avoids driving or being a passenger, which has led to missed meetings and campaign events, impacting both his professional obligations and personal relationships. The strain on their marriage is palpable as John becomes increasingly isolated, convinced that others can see the trauma just by looking at him. What frightens John most is the uncertainty of whether he will ever be able to fully recover from this experience. He feels that his character flaws may have contributed to the accident and worries about how it might affect his public image and political career. These negative appraisals have made him hyper-vigilant, always on guard against potential dangers. John finally sought help when his wife expressed her concerns about his declining mental health and urged him to seek professional support. He is hopeful that with the right guidance, he can regain a sense of control over his life and alleviate some of the distressing symptoms. Despite his fears, John has started to recognize the importance of addressing his trauma and finding ways to cope more effectively.
